clue.text: Mistake of huge proportions, a team in red wearing white start ill-prepared

parts.note: a goof is a blunder
very large, so fat

indicators.note: the team is dressed in the wine, so these letters sit within the white wine

parts.note: hock is a white Rhine wine
LFC, Liverpool Football Club, who play in red

explanation.surface: A giant blunder by a football side in red who turn out in white, kicking off unprepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' is a wine, not a kit colour, and 'wearing' puts the team inside it. Liverpool are an English football club known for red shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes acting prematurely, before being properly ready, like a gun firing from a half-cocked position.

clue.text: Offensive type first joins up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class
knits means joins together, as broken bones do

explanation.surface: A rude fellow is the first to sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinkpot is a slang term for a nasty, objectionable person.

clue.text: Give up source of life, did you say?

indicators.note: a question about what was spoken signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a seed is where a plant's life begins

explanation.surface: Someone half-hears a mention of the origin of life and asks whether to surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a point is to yield or surrender it.

clue.text: Wicket! Sussex opener trapped by bowler on fire — is he out?

indicators.note: the wicket and opener are caught inside the word for burning

parts.note: something on fire is hot
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

indicators.note: the opening letter, as a batsman who opens the innings

parts.note: a bowler is a hat

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a Sussex opening batsman is caught leg before by a fiery bowler, and the fielders appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' is a hat here, not a cricketer. 'How's that?' is the appeal fielders shout to the umpire; Sussex is an English county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket appeal asks the umpire whether the batsman has been dismissed.

clue.text: See 6
Actor in heap beginning to hurt during dance

indicators.note: the heap and the start of hurt happen in the middle of the dance

parts.note: the Charleston is a 1920s dance
a ton, as in tons of something, a heap

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An actor in a pile-up starts to feel pain mid-dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlton Heston was an American film star, known for Ben-Hur.

clue.text: Arab country after uprising has sealed fate when shelled

indicators.note: the country holds the inner letters within it
in a down clue, an uprising turns the letters to read upwards

parts.note: Iraq is a Middle Eastern country

indicators.note: shelling removes the outer letters of the word fate

explanation.surface: After a revolt, an Arab nation's destiny is fixed by bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has sealed' puts the core of fate inside the country, making IRATAQ, which 'after uprising' turns to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Qatari is a native of Qatar, a Gulf state whose people are Arabs.

clue.text: Might Beelzebub get his skates on then? Never!

definitions.text: Might Beelzebub get his skates on then?
definitions.meaning: the Devil could only go skating when his fiery domain turned to ice
an emphatic refusal, meaning not at any time

explanation.surface: A joking question about when the Devil might go ice skating, answered with a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an impossible moment, so it means not ever.

clue.text: Brutally honest person steals? Exactly!

indicators.note: the person takes the scrambled letters inside

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one should'

indicators.note: brutally treated, the word honest is battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A frank individual is accused of theft and agrees: precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely, as a bet on the nose hits the exact result.

clue.text: Scrub cooker hard

parts.note: heat is what cooks the food
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An instruction to clean an oven thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrub' looks like a verb about cleaning; it is scrubland.
explanation.definitionFit: Heath is open land covered with low shrubs, which is scrubland.

clue.text: I hope piano players passed

parts.note: fingers are what play the piano keys
crossed means passed over, as a road

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the pianists have passed their exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase, or making the gesture, expresses a wish for good luck.

clue.text: Come down after end of flight and what should I do? Land!

indicators.note: the falling word is placed after the other pieces
the final letter of the word flight

parts.note: er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure what to do
rain comes down

explanation.surface: A nervous pilot at the end of a flight asks what to do and is told to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down' and 'Land' both look like flying instructions; land is the noun, ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Range of tennis player on the backhand

indicators.note: a backhand stroke goes the other way, so the letters are read in reverse
the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Describing a tennis player's reach on the backhand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' sounds like a tennis player's reach but is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: Wife after skirts in Kuwait, in precarious situation — don't be hasty!

indicators.note: the skirts and wife go inside the risky position

parts.note: being on thin ice is a risky position

indicators.note: the wife comes after the skirts
the outer edges of the word Kuwait

explanation.surface: A man chasing skirts in Kuwait with a wife at home is told to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' is not about women: 'skirts in' takes the edges of Kuwait, and 'in' then places them with the wife inside the risky position.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider before acting is the opposite of being hasty.

clue.text: All those marked for dispatch left inside this, it getting shifted

indicators.note: the left letter goes within the rearranged words
the words this and it are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: An assassin's roster, with a name added in and rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting shifted' rearranges the two words into HITIST, and 'inside' puts L within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit list names people targeted for killing, that is for dispatch.

clue.text: Man who's determined to cultivate derision

indicators.note: to cultivate is to work over, so the word derision is reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A resolute man sets out to foster mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironside is a person of great resolve, a nickname for Cromwell and his troopers.

clue.text: Most important money reaches Arab League leaders

parts.note: a cent is a coin

indicators.note: the leading letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Crucial funds arrive at the heads of the Arab League.
explanation.definitionFit: Central means principal or chief, of first importance.

clue.text: Put cryptically, made fishy?

definitions.meaning: turned into a cod, a whimsical coinage

explanation.surface: Something said in code is made to look suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Codified usually means set out as a system, here taken as put into code; jokingly, made into cod.

clue.text: Further study in theology faculty

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
vision is the faculty of sight

explanation.surface: Postgraduate work within a university's divinity department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests a university department; it is a sense, sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Revision is going over material again before an exam.

clue.text: Painting car seats green originally, I love blue

indicators.note: the car takes the other letters in as passengers

parts.note: Lada is a Russian car make

indicators.note: the opening letter of green

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so CON

explanation.surface: Someone admires a car whose upholstery was green but now loves blue.
explanation.definitionFit: La Gioconda is the Italian name for Leonardo's Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Huge figure has to travel into Yorkshire town, shortly

indicators.note: the travel word goes inside the shortened town
cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Goole is a port town in East Yorkshire
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A big number of people must journey to a northern town briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A googol is ten to the power of a hundred, an enormous number.

clue.text: Top Chinese food, massive plateful?

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: noodles are a staple of Chinese cooking

explanation.surface: Praise for excellent Chinese cuisine served in a large portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective praising the food; it is an instruction to remove the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles means a great quantity, as a heaped plate holds.

clue.text: See 8
See 11
Divine figure and character in audition?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the pieces are as heard

parts.note: the number four followed by the letter C

explanation.surface: A god, a number and a role tried out at a stage audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like a noun or adjective; it is the verb, to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict by insight, which is to see what is coming.

clue.text: Damn sunrises!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: Someone cursing early mornings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of annoyance.

clue.text: Host Native American daughter

parts.note: the Crow are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American woman's daughter hosts a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large number of people, a throng.

clue.text: Conductor waiting to take charge, got on

parts.note: elect after a title, as in president-elect, means chosen but not yet in office
rode, as one gets on and rides a horse or bus

explanation.surface: A bus conductor, about to take over, climbed aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' and 'charge' suggest a bus or orchestra; it is an electrical part.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.
